title: European integration (ECSC to the European Union)
summary: Belgium, France, West Germany, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands signed the Treaty of Paris on 18 April 1951, creating the European Coal and Steel Community under the Schuman Plan, run by a High Authority. The Treaties of Rome of 1957 added a common market, the European Economic Community, and Euratom. The Maastricht Treaty, in force from 1 November 1993, founded the European Union on these communities with new cooperation in foreign policy and justice; the 2007 Lisbon Treaty made Parliament an equal law-maker with the Council in most fields.

uncertainty.note: Spans the signing of the Treaty of Paris establishing the European Coal and Steel Community on 18 April 1951 to the entry into force of the Maastricht Treaty creating the European Union on 1 November 1993.

where.historical_name: Paris, France (signing place of the 1951 Treaty of Paris establishing the ECSC)

importance.justification: Built supranational institutions that now govern much of Europe’s law and trade (R3 D3 T2 L3).

related.because: The Maastricht Treaty's entry into force in 1993 created the European Union, forming the culminating constitutional milestone of post-war integration.

beats.caption: The Treaty of Paris is signed in 1951, pooling coal and steel production under Europe's first supranational community.
The Maastricht Treaty enters into force in 1993, formally establishing the European Union on top of the European Communities.
